snippet.title: Run Your Own Agentic AI? 🦙 Full Ollama Setup + Hermes Workflow
snippet.description:
How can I run my own AI, on my computer, without sending data (or money) to others? It's easier than you think! Local models are getting incredibly powerful and running them takes less time & effort than ever before. Today, I'll walk through why & how to run local LLMs with Ollama, including tips on how to connect to Agentic AI like Hermes Agent ✨ https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GL67DEf2nyI
My Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/c/wanderloots

Running AI agents can be helpful... but also costly, both in terms of money & data. When you connect your agent to a cloud llm like Claude, Gemini, or ChatGPT, you pay for it. Running a local model with a tool like Ollama lets you 1) pay nothing & 2) keep your data secure. 

This local setup matters especially in situations where you want to keep your information private, like note-taking, client work, or business data. Running a local model gives you the power of an LLM, without the fear of sending your data to third parties. 

One of my favourite setups is using a local model to connect to Obsidian, my personal knowledge management system (second brain), so I can chat with my notes but be confident that my information is not leaving my computer. I can also use a local AI to run my LLM wiki, a way to extract information and build a personalized wikipedia from sources I curate. More on LLM Wiki here: https://youtu.be/n4EVksU_EOs

New local models like Gemma4 come in all shapes & sizes to accommodate the computer you're running. You can use the Gemma4:e4b comfortably on most computers, which is why I use it in today's example. 

You can run a local model and connect it to your agent of choice to have a free, private, and local agentic AI system. While I'm using Ollama in today's video, this workflow and concept applies to any local AI platform (LM Studio, Llama cpp, unsloth, etc.). Similarly, while I use Hermes Agent in today's example (by Nous Research), this workflow applies to any Agentic AI (OpenClaw, Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Cursor, Windsurf, etc.). 

There are even specialized local models you can run that enable you to code for free!

I hope you enjoy! ✨

Building a powerful PC for local AI agents requires a different approach than a typical gaming setup. We focus on specific hardware, especially the graphics card's VRAM, which is crucial for running a local llm effectively. This video guides you through how to build a pc optimized for AI, highlighting components like the RTX 4060 Ti with 16GB of VRAM and how to use Ollama for command-line AI operations. Forget cloud-based models; discover the power of your own pc build.

VRAM is the single most important spec for any local AI PC build, and most people are buying the wrong GPU because of it. In this video, I break down the exact hardware you need at 3 budget tiers ($1,200 to $5,000+) to run models like Qwen3, DeepSeek R1, and Llama locally with Ollama, covering both PC and Mac paths.

I also cover which model formats to use (GGUF vs AWQ), how quantization works, and why local AI is your best move for privacy, cost control, and uptime in 2026.

Whether you're running AI coding assistants, document analysis, or building agent workflows with n8n, this guide shows you exactly what to buy and what to skip.
